candidates.change_summary: Replace assignment owner = _owner; with owner = msg.sender; so setOwner assigns the caller instead of the provided _owner.
Replace assignment owner = _owner; with owner = address(0); so setOwner always clears owner to the zero address.
Delete the assignment owner = _owner; so setOwner no longer changes owner (owner remains unchanged after call).
Replace require(msg.sender == owner); with require(msg.sender != owner); in onlyOwner, reversing the guard so only non-owners can call setOwner.
Delete the require check inside onlyOwner, effectively removing the ownership restriction so anyone may call setOwner.
Replace require(msg.sender == owner); with require(tx.origin == owner); so the guard checks transaction origin instead of immediate caller.
Change the returned boolean from true to false so setOwner completes but returns false.
Return the previous owner (always false converted) by returning the equality check result instead of true; this will differ when owner changed to same or different address.

Alter onlyOwner modifier to always allow (no require) so setOwner can be called by non-owner; return value of setOwner may differ because original would have reverted for non-owner callers but here returns true on completion, changing observed return for such callers.
Removed the onlyOwner check by deleting the modifier from the function signature so any caller can change owner.
Changed assignment to set owner to msg.sender instead of the provided _owner so caller becomes owner regardless of argument.
Added a different assignment: set owner to the zero address, making owner always the zero address after call.
Tightened the require so only a hardcoded different address (zero address) is allowed, preventing original owner from calling setOwner and thus changing observable behavior.
